deed: מגן דוד אדום מפעיל את שירות הדם הלאומי ואת מוקד החירום 101
title: Magen David Adom: From a Hut in Tel Aviv in 1930 to the 101 Dispatch Center and the Blood Service of All of Israel

trailer.text: Magen David Adom is Israel's official ambulance service, its blood service and its disaster rescue agency.
In the Land of Israel under the Mandate, there were no first aid or ambulance services.
According to the timeline of MDA's donor organization, on June 7, 1930, seven doctors in Tel Aviv set up an emergency medical service, in a single room in a dilapidated hut.
Today MDA operates the 101 emergency dispatch center and the National Blood Services, and it supplies all of Israel's blood.
As of 2021, the dispatch center receives about 2.7 million medical emergency calls a year.

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: The American Red Cross International Humanitarian Service Award

paragraphs.text: Under the British Mandate, Jews had no nationwide medical services.
In the Land of Israel there were no first aid or ambulance services.
In 1929 Arabs attacked in deadly riots, and the Jewish towns then lacked even the most elementary first-aid services.
Some sources trace the roots of the idea to before 1930.

stations.title: A Hut on the Corner of Rothschild and Nahalat Benyamin

paragraphs.text: On June 7, 1930, medical professionals met in Tel Aviv, under the leadership of Dr. Meshulam Levontin.
They met to discuss the need for a rapid medical response service.
On that day MDA was founded, as a one-room emergency medical service in a dilapidated hut.
The hut stood on the corner of Rothschild and Nahalat Benyamin streets.
The sources tell in different ways who founded the organization.

stations.title: First Ambulance, Branches and a Law

paragraphs.text: Shortly after its founding, MDA opened its first first-aid course.
In 1931 the first ambulance set out.
After Tel Aviv, MDA groups were also formed in Haifa and Jerusalem.
In 1935 the groups united into a national emergency medical organization, which served the public and the Haganah.
It had several dozen volunteers and a small truck converted into an ambulance.
During the second wave of riots, in 1936–1939, MDA grew.
It cared for the wounded and gave first-aid training to the Haganah and the auxiliary police.
In Tel Aviv, a cornerstone was laid for MDA's new headquarters.
On July 12, 1950, the Knesset passed the Magen David Adom Law.
Under the law, MDA serves as Israel's national Red Cross society, in accordance with the Geneva Conventions.
The law did not include government funding, so American donors stepped up their efforts to supply MDA with equipment.
According to Kol Zchut, MDA is the national rescue organization recognized by law in Israel since the beginning of the state.
According to Ynet, MDA is committed to treating anyone in need, regardless of religion, race, nationality or gender.

stations.title: 101: From the Call to the Ambulance

paragraphs.text: In routine times MDA operates ambulances and mobile intensive care units, which provide advanced life support in emergencies, including resuscitation.
Behind every call to the 101 dispatch center is a call taker with medical training, a medic or paramedic.
The call taker gathers critical information and at the same time helps the caller.
The call taker asks for a name and phone number, so that MDA can call the caller back if the call is disconnected.
A caller who cannot explain where they are can receive an SMS or WhatsApp message with a link for sharing their location.
The dispatch center can also receive pictures and video from the scene from callers.
According to MDA, those who speak English, Russian, Arabic or another language can be transferred to a medically trained staff member who speaks their language.
According to an article written in cooperation with MDA, in the 1990s MDA began planning one of the first comprehensive dispatch systems in the world.
Maj. Gen. (res.) Yochanan Gur supervised the development of an in-house system called "Yoram".
The system identifies the closest responder, a paramedic in an ambulance, a medic on a motorcycle or a nearby volunteer, and dispatches them automatically.
Around the start of the millennium, MDA launched a nationwide network of volunteer first responders that operates 24/7.
According to Prof. Eli Jaffe, MDA deputy director for community, less than 10 seconds pass from the moment a call is answered until an ambulance is on the road.

According to a Jerusalem Post article written in cooperation with MDA, the network of first-responder volunteers operating 24/7 shaved critical minutes off response times and saved thousands of lives.

stations.title: The Blood of the Whole Country

paragraphs.text: MDA organizes blood donations, tests and classifies the units, and prepares blood components and plasma.
It maintains reserves for emergencies and supplies blood to hospitals.
MDA supplies all of Israel's blood.
MDA also operates the National Human Milk Bank.
In March 2015 the Atlanta-based Marcus Foundation donated $25 million to build a new blood services center in Ramla.

According to MDA's American donor organization, on May 2, 2022, the Marcus Center, the world's first underground, shielded national blood center, was dedicated in Ramla; it was built almost entirely with American support.
It was built almost entirely with American support.
In the Second Lebanon War, in 2006, MDA treated more than 2,600 victims.
It supplied more than 20,000 blood units and brought humanitarian aid to more than 30,000 people in bomb shelters.
In the 2009 Gaza war, MDA reached 1,180 rocket attacks and treated 770 casualties.
In wartime MDA uses sensor-based systems that can provide information about missile impact sites.
On October 7, 2023, the first calls came at dawn, and within minutes the 101 dispatch center was overwhelmed.
According to a Ynet video, the process remained the same, but the operational capacity in the field and in the dispatch centers doubled within minutes.
According to MDA Director General Eli Bin, the teams treated nearly 1,000 wounded people that day, and the blood services collected about 5,000 units of blood.
According to Bin, seven MDA personnel were murdered, two were critically wounded and many more were harmed while trying to reach the wounded.
That day 14 ambulances were damaged, and three of them were entirely destroyed.

stations.title: The Fleet, the People and the Recognition

paragraphs.text: According to the Jerusalem Post, MDA today operates nearly 2,000 rescue vehicles, 650 emergency motorcycles and 250 rapid-response cars.
According to the same source, it also has five helicopters, five urgent-care ambulances and two rescue boats.
MDA operates on land, in the air and at sea.
Each year, MDA trains tens of thousands of volunteers, medical workers, youth and public figures in first aid and CPR.
MDA's 96th anniversary event was held at the national headquarters in Ramla.
8-year-old Yosef Cohen of Asael was recognized: MDA responders identified that his severe headache was a life-threatening condition.
Daniel Suissa of Petah Tikvah survived cardiac arrest after a neighbor began CPR guided by MDA dispatchers.
Kobi Hershtal, an MDA volunteer and IDF soldier, was critically wounded in Gaza, and his life was saved in part through emergency transfusions of whole blood.
Jeffrey Green, 62, of Beersheva, who recently donated his 100th unit of blood, received special recognition.
According to Director General Eli Bin, MDA has become one of the most advanced emergency medical organizations in the world.
According to JNS, the 96th anniversary event was held at the national headquarters in Ramla

stations.title: The Emblem and the Place in the Red Cross

paragraphs.text: According to the Jewish Press, the Red Cross continues to refuse to recognize the Magen David as a legitimate symbol, although it officially recognized the Red Crescent in 1929.
On June 22, 2006, the International Red Cross recognized MDA, and it was admitted as a full member of the International Federation.

disagreements.question: When did the idea of MDA begin?

versions.says: According to Israel Education, in 1915, when Dr. Moses Erlanger founded an association to provide medical aid to Jews who were wounded and captured in the First World War
According to the Jewish Virtual Library, at a meeting in Philadelphia in October 1918, attended by Ben-Gurion, Golda Meir and Henrietta Szold
According to the Jewish Press, the American-Israel Numismatic Association apparently considers 1919 the year of founding
According to American Friends of Magen David Adom, MDA was founded on June 7, 1930
According to American Friends of Magen David Adom, seven Israeli doctors
According to the Jewish Press, nurse Karen Tenenbaum, who assembled seven Jewish doctors and to whom the birth of MDA is most frequently credited
According to Ynet, medical professionals who met under the leadership of Dr. Meshulam Levontin
Meshulam Levontin, who founded the organization as a volunteer association with one branch in Tel Aviv

disagreements.question: When did the first ambulance set out?

versions.says: According to Ynet, in January 1931
According to the Jewish Press, on June 24, 1931, on a trip from Levontin's home to the home of Tel Aviv mayor Meir Dizengoff

disagreements.question: When was the Haifa branch opened?

versions.says: According to the Jewish Virtual Library, in 1931, and Jerusalem in 1934
According to the Jewish Press, in 1933, and Jerusalem in 1934

disagreements.question: When was the cornerstone laid for the headquarters in Tel Aviv?

versions.says: According to the Jewish Press, in January 1936
According to Israel Education, in December 1934

disagreements.question: How many vehicles and ambulances does MDA have?

versions.says: According to the Jerusalem Post, nearly 2,000 rescue vehicles, plus 650 motorcycles and 250 rapid-response cars
According to the Jewish Virtual Library, over 500 vehicles in ambulances and mobile intensive care units

disagreements.question: How many helicopters does MDA operate?

versions.says: According to the Jerusalem Post, five
According to a Times of Israel blog, two medevac helicopters, alongside a life support boat on the Sea of Galilee

disagreements.question: How many employees and volunteers does MDA have?

versions.says: According to the Jewish Virtual Library, some 990 paid employees and some 6,000 volunteers, most of whom are an emergency reserve force
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, 1,500 employees in 2006, and more than 5,000 volunteers in 1991 and 10,000 in 2006

unknowns.text: According to the Jewish Press, South African President Paul Kruger funded an enterprise at its beginning and permitted an ambulance corps to use the Magen David as its emblem, but the sources here do not explain how this relates to MDA in the Land of Israel

claims.text: מגן דוד אדום הוא שירות האמבולנסים הרשמי של ישראל, שירות הדם וסוכנות ההצלה באסונות.

claims.text: בארץ ישראל תחת המנדט לא היו שירותי עזרה ראשונה או אמבולנסים, והדבר הפך לבעייתי במיוחד אחרי מהומות 1929.
claims.quote: had neither first aid nor ambulance services, which became particularly problematic after the murderous Arab riots of 1929

claims.text: מד"א הוקם ב-7 ביוני 1930 בתל אביב בידי שבעה רופאים ישראלים, כשירות רפואי חירום בחדר אחד בצריף רעוע.
claims.quote: Magen David Adom (MDA) was founded on June 7, 1930, in Tel Aviv by seven Israeli doctors who set up a one-room emergency medical service in a dilapidated hut.

claims.text: מד"א מפעיל אמבולנסים, יחידות טיפול נמרץ, מסוקי אוויר, את מוקד החירום 101, שירותי הדם הלאומיים ואת הבנק הלאומי לחלב אם.
claims.quote: operating ambulances, intensive care units, medevac helicopters, the 101 emergency dispatch center, the National Blood Services and the National Human Milk Bank

claims.text: מד"א מכשיר אלפי חובשים מדי שנה, מספק את כל הדם בישראל ופועל ביבשה, באוויר ובים.
claims.quote: It trains thousands of medics each year, supplies all of Israel’s blood, and responds by land, air, and sea.

claims.text: ביתו הראשון של מד"א היה צריף רעוע בפינת רחוב רוטשילד ונחלת בנימין.
claims.quote: MDA's first home was a dilapidated hut on the corner of Rothschild and Nahalat Benyamin streets

claims.text: תחת המנדט הבריטי לא היו ליהודים שירותי רפואה בהיקף כלל-ארצי.
claims.quote: Under the British Mandate of 1920, Jews had no territorial-wide medical services.

claims.text: ביישובים יהודיים תחת המנדט הבריטי חסרו שירותי עזרה ראשונה בסיסיים ביותר בזמן שערבים תקפו במהומות קטלניות ב-1929.

claims.text: לפי אתר Israel Education, הרעיון לשירות רפואי דחוף לקהילה היהודית החל ב-1915, כשד"ר משה ארלנגר הקים אגודה לסיוע רפואי ליהודים שנפצעו ונפלו בשבי במלחמת העולם הראשונה.

claims.text: לפי הסרטון, ב-7 באוקטובר התהליך נשאר זהה אך היכולת המבצעית בשטח ובמוקדים הוכפלה תוך דקות.
claims.quote: The underlying emergency process remained the same that morning, according to the video, but the operational capacity in the field and dispatch centers doubled within minutes.

claims.text: לדברי מנכ"ל מד"א אלי בין, צוותי מד"א טיפלו ביום אחד בכמעט 1,000 פצועים.
claims.quote: Our teams treated nearly 1,000 wounded people in a single day

claims.text: לדברי בין, שירותי הדם של מד"א אספו באותו יום כ-5,000 מנות דם.
claims.quote: Our blood services collected about 5,000 units of blood that day alone

claims.text: לדברי בין, שבעה אנשי מד"א נרצחו, שניים נפצעו אנושות ורבים נוספים נפגעו בניסיון להגיע לפצועים.
claims.quote: Seven MDA personnel were murdered,” Bin adds. “Two were critically wounded, and many more were harmed while trying to reach the wounded.

claims.text: ב-7 באוקטובר 14 אמבולנסים ניזוקו, שלושה מהם נהרסו כליל.
claims.quote: In addition to the devastating human losses, 14 ambulances sustained damage, with three entirely destroyed.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, מד"א מפעיל כיום כמעט 2,000 רכבי הצלה, 650 אופנועי חירום, 250 רכבי תגובה מהירה, חמש מסוקים, חמישה אמבולנסי טיפול דחוף ושתי סירות הצלה.
claims.quote: Today, MDA operates nearly 2,000 rescue vehicles, 650 emergency motorcycles, 250 rapid-response cars, five helicopters, five urgent-care ambulances, and two rescue boats.

claims.text: מד"א מכשיר מדי שנה עשרות אלפי מתנדבים, עובדי רפואה, בני נוער ואנשי הציבור בעזרה ראשונה והחייאה.
claims.quote: MDA also trains tens of thousands of volunteers, medical workers, youth and members of the public each year in first aid and CPR.

claims.text: אירוע יום השנה ה-96 נערך במטה הארצי של מד"א ברמלה.
claims.quote: Held at the organization’s national headquarters in Ramla, the event on Sunday evening brought together patients reunited with the teams that saved their lives

claims.text: יוסף כהן בן ה-8 מעסאל זכה להכרה: מגיבי מד"א זיהו שכאב הראש החמור שלו הוא מצב מסכן חיים.
claims.quote: Among those recognized was 8-year-old Yosef Cohen of Asael, whose life was saved after MDA responders identified his severe headache as a life-threatening emergency

claims.text: דניאל סויסה מפתח תקווה שרד דום לב אחרי ששכן, בהדרכת מוקדני מד"א, התחיל החייאה.
claims.quote: Attendees also heard the story of Daniel Suissa of Petah Tikvah, who survived cardiac arrest after a neighbor, guided by MDA dispatchers, began CPR

claims.text: חייו של קובי הרשטל, מתנדב מד"א וחייל צה"ל שנפצע אנושות בעזה, ניצלו בין היתר בעזרת עירויי דם מלא דחופים.
claims.quote: his life was saved in part through emergency transfusions of whole blood

claims.text: ג'פרי גרין בן ה-62 מבאר שבע, שתרם לאחרונה את יחידת הדם ה-100 שלו, זכה להערכה מיוחדת.
claims.quote: A special recognition was presented to Jeffrey Green, 62, of Beersheva, who recently donated his 100th unit of blood.

claims.text: לדברי מנכ"ל מד"א אלי בין, הארגון הפך לאחד מארגוני שירותי הרפואה הדחופה המתקדמים בעולם.
claims.quote: Magen David Adom has become one of the most advanced emergency medical service organizations in the world,

claims.text: לפי המאמר, הצלב האדום ממשיך לסרב להכיר במגן דוד כסמל לגיטימי, אף שהכיר רשמית בסהר האדום המוסלמי ב-1929.
claims.quote: the IRC continues to refuse to recognize the Magen David as a legitimate symbol even though it officially recognized the Muslim

claims.text: לפי המאמר, היא כינסה קבוצה של שבעה רופאים יהודים ב-7 ביוני 1930.
claims.quote: she assembled a group of seven Jewish doctors

claims.text: לפי ספריית המקורות היהודית, שירותי האמבולנסים וניידות הטיפול הנמרץ כוללים מעל 500 כלי רכב.
claims.quote: Ambulance and mobile-intensive-care-unit services, with over 500 vehicles in the MDA Fleet.

claims.text: לפי הבלוג, למד"א סירה לתמיכת חיים בכנרת ושני מסוקי מדווק.
claims.quote: an emergent life support boat in the Sea of Galilee, and two Medevac helicopters

claims.text: לפי ספריית המקורות היהודית, מד"א מופעל בידי כ-990 עובדים בשכר.
claims.quote: Magen David Adom is operated by some 990 paid employees

claims.text: לפי ספריית המקורות היהודית, מד"א מופעל גם בידי כ-6,000 מתנדבים, שרובם כוח מילואים המופעל בחירום או בצורך מיוחד.
claims.quote: and by some 6,000 volunteers (youth and adult). Most of the latter comprise a reserve force to be activated in times of emergency or special need.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, מד"א העסיק 1,500 עובדים ב-2006, וכוח המתנדבים מנה יותר מ-5,000 ב-1991 ו-10,000 ב-2006.
claims.quote: mda employed 1,500 workers in 2006, while its volunteer force numbered more than 5,000 in 1991 and 10,000 in 2006.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, נשיא דרום אפריקה פאול קרוגר, שמימן את המיזם בראשיתו, התיר לחיל האמבולנסים להשתמש במגן דוד כסמל במקום הצלב האדום הרגיל.
claims.quote: South African President Paul Kruger, who provided initial funding for the enterprise, granted permission to the corps to use the Magen David as its emblem instead of the standard red cross.

claims.text: נכון ל-2021 מגיעות למוקד כ-2.7 מיליון שיחות חירום רפואיות בשנה.
claims.quote: In 2021, more than 2.7 million calls were fielded.

claims.text: הכרה: פרס השירות ההומניטרי הבינלאומי של הצלב האדום האמריקני
claims.quote: received the American Red Cross’ International Humanitarian Service Award

claims.text: המקורות מספרים בדרכים שונות מי הקים את הארגון.
claims.quote: while others attribute it to a nurse named Karen Tenenbaum

claims.text: המקורות מספרים בדרכים שונות מי הקים את הארגון.
claims.quote: Dr. Meshulam Levontin, commander of the medical unit of the Zion Mule Corps during World War I

claims.text: ב-22 ביוני 2006 הכיר הצלב האדום הבינלאומי במד"א, והוא התקבל כחבר מלא בפדרציה הבינלאומית.
claims.quote: On June 22, the Society was recognized by the International Committee of the Red Cross

claims.text: משולם לבונטין, שהקים את הארגון כאגודת מתנדבים עם סניף אחד בתל אביב
claims.quote: The leader of the founding group was Levontin (1886-1957), who had studied medicine at Moscow University,

claims.text: משולם לבונטין, שהקים את הארגון כאגודת מתנדבים עם סניף אחד בתל אביב
claims.quote: They decided to establish a quick response volunteer emergency medical association

quote_translations.c27: Magen David Adom in Israel is the national rescue organization recognized by law in Israel, since the beginning of the establishment of the state.
quote_translations.c28: Operating ambulances and mobile intensive care units, to provide advanced life support in medical emergencies, including resuscitation treatments
quote_translations.c29: Organizing blood donations, testing and classifying the units, preparing blood components and plasma, maintaining reserves of blood and its components for emergencies and supplying them to hospitals
